title.en: quantifiers: some, any, much, many, a few, a little, each, every

explain.ko: 수량 표현은 셀 수 있는 명사와 셀 수 없는 명사에 따라 달라집니다. 셀 수 있는 명사 복수: many, a few, few, several. 셀 수 없는 명사: much, a little, little. 둘 다: some, any, a lot of, enough, most, no. some은 긍정문과 권유·부탁에, any는 부정문과 의문문에 씁니다. a few / a little은 '조금 있다(충분하다는 느낌)', few / little은 '거의 없다'입니다. each는 하나하나, every는 모두를 뜻하고 둘 다 단수 동사를 씁니다.
explain.en: Quantifiers depend on whether the noun is countable or uncountable. Countable plural: many, a few, few, several. Uncountable: much, a little, little. Both: some, any, a lot of, enough, most, no. Use some in positive sentences and offers, any in negatives and questions. A few / a little means some (enough); few / little means hardly any. Each means one by one and every means all; both take a singular verb.

notes.ko: a few / a little은 긍정적인 느낌, few / little은 '거의 없음'이라는 부정적 느낌입니다.
notes.en: A few / a little is positive; few / little means hardly any.

notes.ko: many / much는 주로 부정문과 의문문에 쓰고, 긍정문에서는 a lot of를 씁니다.
notes.en: Many / much are mostly used in negatives and questions; in positives use a lot of.

notes.ko: each / every 뒤에는 단수 명사와 단수 동사가 옵니다.
notes.en: Each / every take a singular noun and verb.

prompt.ko: 우리 동네나 집에 있는 것과 없는 것을 수량 표현을 사용해 4문장으로 써 보세요.
prompt.en: Write 4 sentences about what there is and isn't in your neighbourhood or home, using quantifiers.

task.model: There aren't many parks in my neighbourhood. But there are a few cafés. I don't have much time at home, so I get up early every morning. Most of my neighbours are friendly and each one knows the others.

model_trans.ko: 우리 동네에는 공원이 많지 않아요. 하지만 카페는 몇 개 있어요. 나는 집에 시간이 많지 않아서 매일 아침 일찍 일어나요. 대부분의 이웃들은 친절하고 모두 서로를 알아요.
model_trans.en: There aren't many parks in my neighbourhood. But there are a few cafés. I don't have much time at home, so I get up early every morning. Most of my neighbours are friendly and each one knows the others.
